---
title: "Rules and project instructions"
---

Instruction files put durable, human-reviewed context near a project. In this repository, `AGENTS.md` is the common source and `CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md` adapters import it where supported. Antigravity needs its verified project-rules mechanism as well; file names alone do not guarantee discovery.

Precedence is harness-specific. OpenCode traverses project `AGENTS.md` upward and falls back to `CLAUDE.md`; Codex layers root-to-current-directory files with nearer files later; Claude layers `CLAUDE.md` files and managed policy; Antigravity rules have activation modes rather than a documented automatic `AGENTS.md` import. Confirm the installed product's rules page and actual loaded context.

Keep instructions concise: scope, safe-data boundary, commands, conventions, and how to verify. Separate a project rule from a personal/global preference. Ask an agent what it loaded, then inspect the files and documentation rather than trusting its explanation.

Rules are not enforcement. They can be ignored, overridden, or bypassed through a tool. For access control, use least-privilege permissions, a disposable environment, and deterministic checks.

::: {.callout-tip}
Classify repeated knowledge before adding it: one-off prompt, project instruction, global instruction, skill, memory/log, or deterministic script. The smallest correct location is usually easiest to maintain.
:::
